questions.question: Is riding directly alongside another vehicle safe?

options.text: Yes, because you are in a separate lane.
Yes, because it blocks the wind.
No, because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane without knowing you are there.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: It builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: Alcohol leaves your body at about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after an hour passes.

questions.question: Does a DOT-approved helmet limit your vision?

options.text: Yes, it severely limits your vision.
No, it lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: How can you make sure other drivers see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in bad visibility.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on at all times.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?

options.text: It can cause you to lose control.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause you to lose control.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and quickly re-apply it. If your rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Zigzag to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over grooves or gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Do not zigzag to compensate, as this is more dangerous.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind it.
Stop and wait for it to move.
Merge into a different lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a different lane away from it.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, change lanes away from it. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If you drink one alcoholic drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding skills. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose, so it flaps in the wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly.
questions.explanation: A protective jacket should fit snugly so it does not flap, but not so tight that it restricts your movement.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you if you crash. They also keep you comfortable and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles are entering the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Let all traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should riders use mirrors?

options.text: All riders should check mirrors often.
Only the lead rider should check mirrors.
Riders should not check mirrors often because it is distracting.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders should check mirrors often.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, all riders should check their mirrors often. This helps you see riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of a lane helps the car driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers do not look at side mirrors as often as the rearview mirror.
Wind can block the side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers do not look at side mirrors as often as the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror much more than their side mirrors. So it is better to ride in the center of the lane. This way the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will not help. They will just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is even more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding, your boots or shoes should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Your footwear should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Shoelaces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What gives you the best chance of surviving a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: A DOT-approved helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good helmet that fits properly is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, be visible to others, signal your moves, keep space around your bike, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. So wear bright, reflective clothes whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may go through slowly and carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait until the light lets you turn in the direction you want.

questions.question: Why is it good to keep space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: It helps you go faster by following other vehicles.
It gives you more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If something happens, you will have more time to respond and more room to move safely.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of a head or neck injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are a risk when riding, no matter your speed. A good helmet worn correctly greatly reduces this risk.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection you cannot see clearly?

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield to you.
Move to a position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly at an intersection, move your position in the lane so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: What happens if you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
You should flash your lights to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
